1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

3	description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
4	---
5	
6	The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
7	future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
8	by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
9	fields.
10	
11	## Read
12	
13	- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
14	  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
15	  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
16	  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
17	  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
18	- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
19	  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,

68	  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`

104

178	- `horizon inbox complete <id>` — mark an item resolved only when it records work

183	  grasp the result and how it was concluded without opening the logs.

191	  - `--owner <task-id>` / `--mine` keeps the item in one team's inbox instead of
192	    the shared default.
193	  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).
194	  - `--persistent` / `--temporary` just prepend a `[persistent]` / `[temporary]`

196	  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,

198	- `horizon inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body "Short memory title\n\nDurable fact, convention, or dead end."` — record a durable

I restated `pic0Subgroup` membership (`degAt lam t = 0` at every field point) as fibrewise
triviality (`picEtMap C t lam = 1`), proved the equivalence in both directions, and published
it as "a repricing — the degree condition is provably idle at genus 0, what remains has no
degree, no χ, no divisor and no chart". A fresh-context audit refuted it: at genus 0 the two
antecedents are equivalent *for every test and every class*, so the new form is the same
hypothesis with the predicate spelled differently. The degree left the notation, not the
mathematics.

**Why:** the tell was inside my own file and I wrote it myself — the converse
(`rigidity_of_pic0Vanishing`) needs **no genus hypothesis**. A genuinely weaker target does not
round-trip for free. Proving an iff in both directions is precisely the demonstration that the
two sides are one predicate; I used it as evidence of a discount.

**How to apply:** when a reduction's converse is cheap or hypothesis-free, that is a signal the
"reduction" is a change of coordinates. Before calling it a repricing, ask what a consumer can
now do that it could not before. Here the honest answer was narrow and real: `classDeg` carries
five fibre instance binders that do not synthesize through a `def` barrier, so the triviality
spelling makes hypotheses *statable* at a general prime that could not be written down at all.
That is a statability gain, not a smaller obligation — and it was worth saying, unlike the claim
I made. Related: [[measure-the-converse-before-strictly-weaker]],

###### cas-must-use-the-readtree-sha
---
name: cas-must-use-the-readtree-sha
description: commit-tree + update-ref NEW OLD only refuses a stale tree if OLD is the sha read-tree used; re-reading HEAD for the CAS defeats it silently
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

I-1517 prescribes replacing `git commit -m` with `commit-tree` + `update-ref
refs/heads/main NEW OLD`, saying the old-value argument "makes update-ref FAIL
rather than clobber if HEAD moved". I did exactly that and clobbered 13 paths
across two other lanes anyway.

**Why:** update-ref's CAS compares the *ref* to the value **you pass**. I read
`OLD=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` fresh immediately before `write-tree`, so the value
passed was current and the CAS succeeded — while the *tree* was stale, built by a
`read-tree` from an earlier HEAD. A CAS on the ref cannot detect a stale index.
Both spellings look identical at the command line.

**How to apply:** capture OLD **once, before** `read-tree`, and pass that same
value to `read-tree`, `commit-tree -p`, and `update-ref`. Never re-read HEAD in
between. Also: `commit-tree` prints no stat, so adopting it disables the free
tripwire of comparing commit's own printed stat to the pre-commit one — the
post-commit `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat`, read path by path, becomes the only
detector. Related: [[read-tree-commit-race]],
[[read-tree-goes-stale-between-add-and-commit]],

2026-07-31, AJC (`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`), pic-e run 0095 r6. Three
sorry-free theorems from three lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the
project's central `sorry` (`fgaPicardRepresentability`) from the classical
*pointed* FGA theorem — `Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`, 11 declarations, all
axiom-clean. So the arbitrary-field difficulty protection I-0491 deliberately put
on the headline is discharged; what remains is the pointed theorem plus
quasi-projectivity of the representing scheme.

**No row mentioned the other two.** `descent-assembly` listed four open inputs and
three were already discharged elsewhere; the seam docstring's own "what remains"
sentence listed three items, one closed and one *done and called remaining*. Every
row was individually plausible. The composition existed only across them.

**Why per-row checks cannot see it:** a lane records what *it* owes, not what
another lane has since supplied, so rows go stale in the CHEAP direction — they
schedule work that exists — and a list of remaining obligations reads as
self-criticism, so nobody re-tests it. Distributed version of
[[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]].

**The check, and it is cheap:** `#check` the consumer theorem a costing tells you
to aim at, and ask of each *literal binder* "does a producer for exactly this exist
at HEAD?" — not "is this gap open", which is what the row answers. At
`seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree`, three of four were gone and the
fourth was an instance binder no row named. See
[[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]], [[gap-count-vs-gap-cost]].

**Corollary that cost me a withdrawal:** price the composed result against the
weakest antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first
antecedent carried `IsSeparated`, provably free from the conclusion's own
representation — a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports
exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]].

###### tactic-failure-is-not-object-fact

name: tactic-failure-is-not-object-fact
description: "A failing simpa/rw published as \"these two terms do not unify\" becomes a prohibition other lanes obey; the missing step was a `change`"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 69fe1b7e-3708-4eee-bf36-a68e4b749a72

---

pic-c (AJCR 0092 r5) wrote in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to
pic-g: "going through `chi_moduleKSheaf` at the bundled `baseChangeBundle C K` produces the
same object under a different `Over` instance, and the resulting `chi` terms do not unify —
measured". What was actually measured was that **one `simpa` call failed**. Adding a
`change` to the bundled spelling before it makes the route close at *default* heartbeats.
And pic-g's own `Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean` was already doing the "impossible" thing in
the same hour — one grep would have refuted it before it was sent.

**Why:** a failing tactic has two possible causes — the objects really differ, or the tactic
was not given the reduction it needed. Only the first is a fact about the mathematics, and
only the first licenses a prohibition. Publishing the second as the first is worse than
saying nothing, because a "TRAP, MEASURED" note forecloses a working route for every later
round, and nobody re-tests a warning.

**How to apply:** before writing that two terms "do not unify" or that a route is closed,
(1) try `change`/`show` to the other spelling, or `convert ... using 1`, and (2) grep the
tree for a file that already does the thing you are about to prohibit. If a sibling does it,
you are wrong. Say "my `simpa` failed here and I did not chase it" instead — that is true,
costs nothing, and does not stop anyone.

Same session, same shape, two more times: "the converse is absent from the tree" (a landed
lemma proved it in four lines — see [[check-the-statement-not-the-name]]) and a consumer
count belonging to a different object ([[gap-count-vs-gap-cost]]). All three flattered the
work. See also [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]] and

###### degenerate-value-can-be-principled
---
name: degenerate-value-can-be-principled
description: substituting a trivial parameter is not automatically a vacuity — enumerate the conjuncts and name which single one the value kills
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: af9011ed-1e8d-456e-bec3-77aab061db09
  modified: 2026-07-30T04:44:34.374Z
---

A degenerate parameter can be the one where an obligation is PRINCIPLED, not the
one where it is vacuous. The test that tells the two apart is **which conjunct
fails at the next value**.

I have several memories pushing the other way ([[degenerate-case-is-per-clause]],
[[substitute-trivial-value-in-layer-one]], [[nonvacuity-witness-must-satisfy-the-binders]]):
a trivial substitution usually shows a clause is *cheap* without exhibiting an
inhabitant, and whole roadmaps have been mispriced on that conflation. So the
reflex is to distrust it.

**Why:** the reflex is right about the mechanism and wrong as a verdict. In AJCR
run 0092 I built the degree-0 corner of a 7-field colength certificate that had
zero producers at every parameter. Six of the seven fields say a zero module is
free — true at every `n`. Exactly ONE, `rankAtStalk_glued = n`, is what `n = 0`
makes vacuous. That is a degenerate *number in one clause*, not a degenerate
object, and the thing produced was a real certified family over every test ring.
The sharper half: effectivity of a divisor holds at every `n` and pins nothing;
the certificate's degree identity holds at every `n` and pins nothing; their
CONJUNCTION at `0` forces the divisor to be zero, giving uniqueness. Two
individually-free facts, jointly decisive at one value — invisible if you price
them separately ([[gap-count-vs-gap-cost]]).

**How to apply:** before dismissing *or* believing a degenerate parameter —
(a) enumerate the obligation's conjuncts and name the single one the value kills;
(b) ask whether the value also makes a second, independent fact decisive (if so
it is a theorem, not a vacuity); (c) state which binders the result still needs,
so the transfer question stays visible. Mine needed `Field` twice for uniqueness
and nothing at all for inhabitation — and saying that is what kept the open half
from being read as closed ([[witness-site-makes-consequent-free]]).

###### ask-what-the-action-is-defined-as

name: ask-what-the-action-is-defined-as
description: "A \"these two predicates agree\" obligation is free when one side's structure was built by transporting the other's natural transformation; check the definition before pricing"
metadata:

I introduced `IsInvariantMatch` as a named hypothesis (AJC descent route, campaign G1),
priced "a model at a nontrivial automorphism" as the open question, and filed a caveat
that its satisfiability was not content. Next session I **proved it free at every
extension** — no finiteness, no separability, no `IsGalois`.

The obligation said: a class's representing morphism is Galois-**equivariant** iff the
class is Galois-**invariant**. But the action it was stated against,
`semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy`, has its γ-component *defined* as
`rep.homEquiv.symm` of the functor action at the universal class. So the two sides were
never independent: apply `rep.homEquiv` to one, use **naturality** of the transported
transformation at the quantified morphism, and you land on the other. Three formal
steps, zero geometry.

**Why:** four rounds of lanes read "the action is free from `rep`" as good news and kept
pricing a match *against* that action as if it were arbitrary. Nobody asked what the
action was **defined as**. A hypothesis relating two objects is suspect the moment one is
constructed from the other — see [[price-the-consumer-carrier]] and
[[find-the-step-that-consumes-the-hypothesis]].

**How to apply:** before budgeting any "predicate A agrees with predicate B" obligation,
read the *definition* of each side's structure. If either is built by transporting a
natural transformation along an equivalence, try naturality at the morphism the predicate
quantifies over before writing it down as an input. And distinguish the genuinely-open
sibling: on the same route `hcov` is a *covering* statement about two objects neither
defined from the other, and it did not fall to this — so "one of the pair was free"
licenses nothing about the other ([[two-refutations-are-not-inhabitation]]).

Corollary for my own prose: closing this falsified three sentences I had written about
it, including one flagged as self-criticism. [[closing-a-residue-falsifies-your-hedges]].

###### measure-the-converse-before-strictly-weaker
---
name: measure-the-converse-before-strictly-weaker
description: "Declining to measure the converse while calling your residue \"strictly weaker\" asserts the very thing you declined to check"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 0d2ea074-9c15-4f46-97aa-fb498a71dffc
  modified: 2026-07-29T19:05:34.986Z
---

Writing "I did NOT prove the converse" as an honest caveat, and "strictly weaker than
X" as the finding, is self-contradictory: the weaker-than claim *is* the converse's
negation. The caveat reads as careful scoping, so consumers keep the strength claim and
discard the doubt. AJCR case (run 0088, `Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce.lean`): I reduced the
Abel-chart fork to a ring-level `RelPicSeparatesDivFamZar`, proved one direction, and
priced it "strictly weaker" in three docstrings and two commit messages on the strength
of its **spelling** — one ring, no test object, no chart, no twist. A fresh-context audit
proved the converse in ~30 lines from one naturality lemma my own two simp lemmas already
implied. The residue was the fork's injectivity *renamed*.

**Why:** fewer binders is a nicer statement to prove *about*, never a smaller thing to
prove. And a quotient in the statement is not automatically a discount — check the
subgroup where the arguments live. Here `relPicMk` quotients by `picFromBase`, which is
trivial at every field test, so the "modulo" bought nothing exactly where the fibrewise
reasoning happens; the residue in fact *implies* injectivity of `picClass`, so it was the
stronger side.

**How to apply:** before writing "strictly weaker"/"strictly easier" anywhere, spend the
20 minutes on the converse — the machinery that let you *state* the reduction is usually
what transports back. If it closes, say "renamed, at unchanged price, and here is what the
obligation IS" — still worth landing, just not a discount. Same session, same file, two
more of the pattern: I cited a declaration (`h0_eq_one_of_relPicSeparates_field`) that was
never written, in the sentence carrying the file's key claim — delete such a sentence, do
not rephrase it, since it asserts a proof exists. And an import-closure finding framed as
"those five files missed something" was equally true of my own file; say "a limitation this
file shares".

Related: [[finish-it-instead-of-pricing-it]], [[absence-census-scoped-to-closure]],
[[nonvacuity-check-can-refute-your-claim]], [[cited-names-need-check-not-grep]].

###### subsumption-claim-is-site-dependent
---
name: subsumption-claim-is-site-dependent
description: "X now closes by inferInstance" is a claim about a file's import closure, and it is often false at the very site being superseded
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

"The old witness is now closed by `inferInstance`" is not a fact about the
declaration — it is a fact about **the file you measure it in**. When a general
producer subsumes a hand-built witness, the sentence is usually placed *at the
witness*, which is exactly where it tends to be false: the new module often
imports the witness's module (for some auxiliary instance), so the reverse import
is a **cycle** and no amount of adding imports fixes it. Sites two hops below the
new module are equally unable to reproduce either direction of the measurement.

**Why:** the measurement is run from the new file, where it passes, and then
written down at the older sites the claim is *about*. This is
[[cited-names-need-check-not-grep]] in the direction of instance synthesis rather
than name resolution, and I reproduced it one file away from a commit whose
message announced fixing another instance of it.

**How to apply:** probe with *exactly the target site's imports* — copy its import
block into a scratch file — before writing a supersession sentence there. If it
fails, say "from any file importing this module" and check whether a cycle makes
it permanent. Then relabel the old proof **generalised, not superseded**: it stays
as the producer where it stands, and often independently as the non-vacuity
witness. Related: [[closing-a-residue-falsifies-your-hedges]],
[[failing-inferinstance-is-not-absence]], [[check-the-statement-not-the-name]].

###### staged-m-unroots-your-module
---
name: staged-m-unroots-your-module
description: "A staged M on the root module deletes your import line, unrooting a file that stays present and byte-identical to HEAD"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 39d5f3a0-9a53-4db5-81ab-2fbcc88d42fa
  modified: 2026-07-31T01:45:39.456Z
---

The shared-index hazard is filed everywhere as staged **deletions**, so every check
built for it asks "is my path staged D" or "is my path present". A staged **M** on
an aggregator/root module defeats all of them: my two new modules were present,
sha256-identical to HEAD, and not staged D — while the staged root module deleted
both `import` lines.

**Why:** losing reachability is as bad as losing the file. An unrooted module is
never compiled by a full build, so it silently stops being checked while every
path-level and content-level verification passes. That is the same failure the
board tracks as a build-reach defect, except manufactured by the index rather than
by an author.

**How to apply:** after committing, in addition to hashing your own paths, run
`git diff --cached HEAD -- <root module> | grep <your-import>`. If your import
appears with a `-`, the next shared-index commit unroots you. Note the stale
`index.lock` may block repairing it — then the only move is to report it loudly.

Related: [[explicit-paths-dont-protect-shared-index]],
[[private-index-does-not-protect-the-message]], [[hash-your-paths-after-committing]],
[[verify-content-not-commit-sha]], [[rooted-sorry-scaffold-breaks-everyone]].

AJC's Cluster D' (the Milne-Kollar replacement for Quot) rests on

inhabiting. Related: [[gap-count-vs-gap-cost]],

and is a **strengthening** whenever the family was introduced so the index could vary per point.

vacuity check sees the difference — the file builds green either way.

On a shared worktree with many parallel lanes, committing through a private index

reverted *module* is loud — the build fails. A reverted **import line**, **docstring** or
**statement** is silent: everything compiles, no linter fires, and the build job count

`∀`-quantifier a reviewer had just refuted; another dropped a module out of the root cone,

1	# LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
2	
3	LeanAG Horizon is a multi-project Lean 4 and Mathlib workspace for formalizing algebraic
4	geometry with [Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon). Its central goal is
5	the algebraic-geometry version of the [Algebraic Jacobian challenge](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian.20challenge/near/587802685),
6	proposed by Christian Merten after Kevin Buzzard's differential-geometry challenge.
7	
8	> [!IMPORTANT]
9	> The workspace develops **two live routes** to the Algebraic Jacobian challenge. Follow the
10	> project named by the active task rather than treating either route as reference-only.
11	>
12	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` continues the ambitious Picard-scheme route, building
13	>   representability by the Milne–Kollár construction of `Pic^r`, then `Pic^0` and the Albanese
14	>   property. Its Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening-stratification substrate is sorry-free
15	>   and still consumed, but the Quot-scheme endgame it was first written for is not the path being
16	>   built. Since 2026-07-28 its headline is stated over an arbitrary base field, with
17	>   representability asked of the étale-sheafified Picard functor and no rational-point hypothesis.
18	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` develops a cleaner curve-specialized route
19	>   from protected target statements.
20	
21	The two projects share mathematical sources and supporting subprojects while keeping independent
22	Lean roots, blueprints, and roadmaps. The rebuild is listed first in the workspace manifest as the
23	default project; explicitly scoped tasks may and do advance the ambitious original route.
24	
25	The [live dashboard](https://axeldlv00.github.io/LeanAlgebraicGeometry/) is the best view of current
26	tasks, commits, session logs, blueprint graphs, and declaration-level progress. A static snapshot
27	is published approximately every 30 minutes; GitHub Pages deployment and caching can add a few
28	minutes before a new snapshot is visible.
29	
30	## Repository Layout
31	
32	| Path | Role |
33	| --- | --- |
34	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` | Cleaner curve-specialized AJC route and workspace default. |
35	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme AJC route (Milne–Kollár representability), maintained by scoped tasks. |
36	| `SubProjects/` | Supporting, extracted, and related-paper formalizations available to the active project. |
37	| `references/` | Shared mathematical sources and retrieval notes. |
38	| `.archon-horizon/` | Workspace state: tasks, roadmap, inbox, run metadata, graphs, and ledger. |
39	| `config.yaml` | Ordered workspace manifest. The rebuild is listed first because it is the primary project. |
40	
41	Each route has its own overview:
42	
43	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md)
44	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md)
45	
46	## Project Map
47	
48	The workspace currently registers these projects, in priority order:
49	
50	| Project | Purpose |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| **`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`** | Cleaner curve-specialized route; default project in the workspace manifest. |
53	| `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme, `Pic^0`, and Albanese route. |
54	| `Line-Bundle-Comparison-Iso` | Extracted line-bundle pullback, tensor, and dual comparison infrastructure. |
55	| `Albanese` | Albanese universal property, rigidity, and rational-map-extension infrastructure. |
56	| `Cech-Cohomology` | Čech computation of higher direct images and its cohomological substrate. |
57	| `GR-Quot-Closure` | Relative Grassmannian and quotient-representability infrastructure. |
58	| `MR0555258-Compactifying-Picard` | Compactifying the Picard scheme (D'Souza), under `SubProjects/RelatedPapersFormalisation/`. |
59	| `Picard-IdentityComponent` | Extracted Picard identity-component and `Pic^0` development. |
60	
61	These member projects remain useful sources of proved APIs, mathematical designs, and failure
62	memory for both main routes.
63	
64	## Working in a Main Project
65	
66	The workspace currently uses Lean and Mathlib `v4.31.0`. Build the project named by the task. For
67	the ambitious Picard-scheme route:
68	
69	```bash
70	cd MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
71	lake build
72	```
73	
74	The rebuild uses the shared workspace package directory at `.lake-packages`, so member projects
75	can reuse the same Mathlib checkout while retaining independent build directories.
76	
77	For workspace-wide exploration, run commands from the repository root:
78	
79	```bash
80	horizon dashboard
81	horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge frontier
82	horizon search "Jacobian Picard representability"
83	```
84	
85	The first command starts the local dashboard. The graph command shows the ranked proof frontier
86	for the active project, and search queries declarations across the workspace and Mathlib.
87	
88	Treat `graph frontier` output as advisory and verify each row in the tree: neither main project has
89	an `hgraph/config.yaml`, so `horizon graph … sync` is a no-op and the stored graph drifts behind
90	landed work (archived inbox item `I-0501`). The scanner also invents declarations from docstring
91	prose, and some arrive marked `sorry`, so the frontier can list nodes that do not exist (archived
92	`I-0472`). Both defects were reproduced and neither was fixed.
93	
94	## Methodology
95	
96	[Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon) coordinates long-running
97	formalization while keeping mathematical and operational state explicit:
98	
99	- **Horizon sessions** implement and verify Lean proofs against concrete tasks.
100	- **Fresh-context reviewers** such as Ground, work-reviewer, and janitor are dispatched at review
101	  and maintenance checkpoints rather than acting as a permanent second driver.
102	- **Blueprint graphs (`hgraph`)** track declaration dependencies, proof status, comments, and the
103	  ranked frontier for each project.
104	- **Roadmap, tasks, and inbox** record strategy, scoped work, cross-session handoffs, and durable
105	  failure memory.
106	- **The workspace ledger** records coherent commits and powers the public dashboard's progress
107	  and session views.
108	
109	Concurrent sessions can share a project's root import file. When adding one
110	import, build the staged root from the ledger's current `HEAD` and insert only
111	that line; do not stage the whole on-disk root, which may contain another
112	session's uncommitted imports.
113	
114	The mathematical blueprint is kept separate from implementation journals. Lean-specific progress
115	and failed approaches belong in graph comments, tasks, or the inbox, while the blueprint remains a
116	timeless account of the mathematics.
117	
118	## Contributing
119	
120	Contributions are welcome, but keep the two routes and task scope explicit:
121	
122	- **AJC proofs and infrastructure:** change only the main project named by the task; share reusable
123	  inputs through the supporting projects when appropriate.
124	- **Protected statements:** do not alter the signatures in the rebuild's `Challenge.lean` or files
125	  covered by `archon-protected.yaml` without prior agreement. Contributions should discharge those
126	  statements, not weaken or reshape them silently.
127	- **Issues and discussions:** include the declaration name and file path, and state whether the
128	  question concerns the statement, naming, proof strategy, or intended use.
129	- **Large changes:** check the live dashboard or open an issue first so work does not duplicate an
130	  active Horizon task.
131	- **Supporting work:** a focused subproject under `SubProjects/` is appropriate when a reusable
132	  dependency needs to be developed independently, but its intended consumer should be the active
133	  rebuild.
134	
135	Clear, stable, mathematical declaration names and warning-free builds are expected. Using the
136	`horizon` CLI is recommended so contributions remain aligned with the workspace manifest,
137	blueprint graph, and ledger conventions.
